query: Deep learning for ECG arrhythmia detection

paper.title: Cardiologist-Level Arrhythmia Detection with Convolutional Neural Networks

summarization.summary: This study presents a 34-layer convolutional neural network designed to detect arrhythmias from single-lead ECGs, claiming cardiologist-level performance on a novel dataset of ~64,121 records. The architecture utilizes residual connections, batch normalization, and ReLU activations to process 30-second signals sampled at 200 Hz. Experimental results demonstrate that the model outperforms board-certified cardiologists in both recall and precision, achieving an aggregate Sequence F1 of 0.776 and Set F1 of 0.809 compared to human scores of 0.719 and 0.751. While excelling in common rhythms like Bigeminy (F1: 0.897), the model significantly underperformed on rare or complex classes such as Ventricular Tachycardia (F1: 0.506) and Early Repolarization (F1: 0.519). Confusion primarily occurred between morphologically similar conditions, including Wenckebach versus AV Block Type II. A key limitation is the explicit exclusion of non-arrhythmic conditions like myocardial infarction and Ventricular Flutter from detection capabilities, which may necessitate multi-lead recordings for accurate diagnosis.

Table 1 also supports the Bigeminy, Ventricular Tachycardia, and Early Atrial Repolarization (EAR) class-level scores and the Wenckebach/Mobitz II confusion; the conclusion explicitly excludes ventricular flutter/fibrillation and myocardial infarction.
